episodes.178268: As an upper low, and accompanying developing surface low,  traversed the region during the morning to early afternoon hours, a few storms produced small hail and strong gusty winds. A Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) appeared to develop and produced strong wind gusts and some damage around Lake Murray and the central Midlands of SC.   Additional convection east of the MCV produced some localized wind damage.
episodes.178393: A rapid increase in moisture/instability associated with a stalled front near the coast eventually shifting north as a warm front led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.178394: A cold front associated with low pressure tracking across the region led to a few showers/thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.178398: A developing early morning squall line ahead of a cold front moving across the Eastern Gulf of Mexico produced an EF-1 tornado in Charlotte County along with few additional 50+ mph sub-severe wind gusts across southwest Florida.
episodes.178399: A developing early morning squall line ahead of a cold front moving across the Eastern Gulf of Mexico produced gusty marine winds across the Tampa Bay Area and Southwest Florida waters.
episodes.178535: Thunderstorms moving offshore from the Brevard and Treasure Coasts produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.178568: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on drainages in Gunnison County. As a result, flooding compromised and led to the failure of a culvert which led to flooding near Bear Creek.
episodes.179337: High shear, low CAPE pre-frontal convection became locally strong to severe during the early morning hours across NE FL.

episodes.179339: Already saturated grounds from 1-3 inches of rain the previous days set the stage for a localized flash flooding event to unfold on April 30th when an additional 2-3 inches of rainfall fell over a period of several hours. A mesoscale moderate to locally heavy rain band with rainfall rates of 0.5 to 1 per hour set up over the NYC metro area during the afternoon of April 30th when a low pressure system was developing to the south of the area.

episodes.179360: A strong low pressure system tracked up the East Coast bringing moderate to locally heavy rainfall across the region on April 30, continuing into the overnight hours on May 1. Rainfall amounts were generally in the 1 to 2 inch range with some localized areas receiving 3 inches. This rainfall was enough to result in some minor flooding across portions of eastern New York, mostly ponding of water on roads or flooding in poor drainage areas.

episodes.179588: A broken line of storms, ahead of a cold front, moved across portions of the region on April 30th. They brought strong, southwesterly winds up to 50mph to Lake Okeechobee and southeastern Florida.
episodes.179651: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, with strong to severe storms affecting a large area of Eastern NC, producing strong damaging wind gusts.
episodes.179681: A cold upper low brought wind damage and small hail.
episodes.179726: A sub 1000 millibar surface low tracked through NC during the early afternoon hours. Showers and thunderstorms developed along a retreating warm front, causing numerous reports of downed trees and wind damage. Some portions of Wilson County saw significant tree damage with the storms as they moved through the area.
episodes.179864: An upper level trough and surface low was expected to push eastward into the Carolinas through the morning and midday hours. Warm sector conditions for Georgia included 500-1000 J/Kg of CAPE & effective shear >35 kts. Mid level lapse rates were expected to exceed 7 C/Km across central GA, indicating further support for damaging winds, hail and a brief tornado being possible. Storm total QPFs of 0.5 to 1.5 were anticipated, with locally higher amounts possible.

A tornado formed over the eastern branch of Lynnhaven River in the City of Virginia Beach. The tornado progressed up River Road as an EF1, passing by the Great Neck Recreation Center. It increased to an EF2 intensity, as it moved into the Chelsea |neighborhood. The tornado continued onto Haversham Close with EF3 intensity. In this area, several homes were shifted off their foundations and roofs and upper walls were completely removed. The tornado then crossed Broad Bay and the eastern portion of Bay Island, clipping Windward Shore Drive as an EF1. It then moved over First Landing State Park and into Fort Story as an EF1, snapping trees, damaging barracks, and damaging several other buildings before moving offshore. Approximately 115 homes were damaged with 11 homes destroyed according to the City of Virginia Beach. Vehicles were overturned and boats were sunk and moved. There were no deaths and no injuries.
